summary: Pinned-model propagation lag at edge causes short 'un-pinned' window and transient fallbacks for NovaRetail
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaRetail) reported intermittent 502/5xx and silent model swap to a fallback variant during a scheduled canary promote of redwood/open-llama-3b-v2. Symptoms occur only for a narrow window (~6s) immediately after control-plane commit; traffic that should be pinned to the promoted version receives the fallback variant.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints experienced degraded quality and higher token cost for ~6s windows during each promote attempt.
- No full outage; error rate spike to ~3% for the tenant during each promote.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (NovaRetail-prod), us-east-1, nodes behind edge-proxy fleet (edge-v4).
- Promote initiated from console rollout API at 2026-03-10T17:02:14Z.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start canary promote of version v2026-03-10T17.
2) Wait for control-plane commit to edge (commit logged at 2026-03-10T17:02:14Z).
3) Generate sustained traffic from customer tenant; sampling shows a 5–7s window where requests are routed to fallback variant despite pin annotation on session token.

Observed behavior:
- Edge logs show commit acknowledgement received by control-plane at 17:02:14Z, but some edge-proxy instances apply the new routing state after a delay (17:02:20Z+).
- Requests from affected connections show pin cookie present but session-handshake at edge returned model_id: fallback-llama-3b, not v2026-03-10T17.
- KV prefix cache warmup completes after the delayed apply, and normal pinned routing resumes.

Expected behavior:
- Pin state should be atomically visible across edge fleet within <1s of commit; no brief window where pin exists but routing falls back.

Logs / evidence:
- Edge-proxy log excerpt (edge-042): [2026-03-10T17:02:14.122Z] received commit token 'promote-42'
- Same node: [2026-03-10T17:02:20.341Z] applied routing snapshot id=8791
- Client trace shows request at 17:02:16.512Z returned variant fallback-llama-3b (trace id trc-33a2).
- Console audit: rollout step 'commit' for tenant nova-retail logged at 17:02:14Z.

Hypothesis / quick notes:
- Control-plane publishes commit, but propagation to edge instances is not synchronized; some proxies enter a state where pin metadata exists in the request but their local route table still references old capacity/fallback routing.
- Session token rotation happening ~every 5s for this tenant (short TTL) may be exposing a race: new token with pin set reaches an edge node that hasn't yet warmed the KV cache or the new model routing map, causing fallback.
- Possible root causes: delayed snapshot apply on edge-proxy (OOM GC stall?), heartbeat backpressure with the dedicated pool, or a race between pin-attach and local route table flush.

Immediate mitigation attempted:
- Rolled back promote on customer request to stop further regressions (console rollback at 17:06:10Z).
- Increased rollout commit quorum to require at least 90% edge apply before accepting promote (temporary control-plane guard).
- Advised customer to increase session-token TTL to 30s while we investigate.

Next steps:
- SRE to collect full edge-proxy apply latency histogram across fleet for the promote window.
- Engineering to audit edge apply path for potential GC/backpressure windows.
- Add additional instrumentation to correlate token issuance timestamp to routing snapshot apply timestamp.
- Plan for a canary test with staged small cohort and forced token TTL extension to validate fix.
comments: 2026-03-10 18:09 - Support (Evelyn Smith): Opened ticket after NovaRetail reported repeated short windows of mixed-model responses during a promote. Customer reports quality drift and cost spike. Provided request traces and edge log excerpts. Assigned to SRE/edge oncall.

2026-03-10 18:27 - SRE (Omar Patel): Observed edge-proxy nodes with delayed routing snapshot apply times; tail latency ~6s on ~4% of nodes. Collecting pprof and GC metrics. Correlating with node-level CPU/heap usage. Marking as Sev1 due to customer impact.

2026-03-10 19:05 - Eng (Jae Park): Hypothesis: snapshot apply blocked by housekeeping task (cache eviction). Requested instrumented build of edge-proxy to log apply start/finish and snapshot size. Will deploy to a small canary group tonight.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Customer (NovaRetail, Alice Moreno): We're seeing this during most promotions; short windows of poor outputs are causing customer complaints. We're willing to hold promotions while you investigate. Thank you for quick action.

2026-03-11 14:45 - SRE (Omar Patel): Collected histogram shows median apply=120ms, 95th=1.2s, 99.9th=6.4s on nodes with older kernel/ebpf probe process; flagged 7 nodes for replacement. Replacing nodes reduced incidents in follow-up dry run.

2026-03-12 11:37 - Eng (Jae Park): Patch candidate: ensure routing snapshot application is prioritized and perform lazy KV warmup rather than blocking pin visibility. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2142. Planning rollout to canary group tomorrow.

2026-03-12 16:02 - Support (Evelyn Smith): Notified customer of planned canary rollout of fix and suggested session-token TTL change as temporary mitigation. Customer approved and requested status updates.

2026-03-13 08:55 - Eng (Jae Park): Canary rollout started (edge-v4-canary cohort). Early telemetry shows apply latency 95th drops to ~450ms and no observed pin->fallback windows in canary traffic over 2h. Continuing rollout and monitoring.

2026-03-13 13:18 - Support (Evelyn Smith): Customer confirms they have not observed further windows during the canary test period. Keeping ticket open until full rollout completes and we validate across dedicated pool.
investigation_notes:
- Edge nodes with older kernel and heavy sidecar telemetry process had higher apply latency.
- Token rotation TTL of 5s for NovaRetail increases exposure window; even small apply delays can surface as fallback.
- Patch focuses on non-blocking snapshot apply and pre-populating route table with pin entries when present in control-plane commit.
- Also adding a rollout guard: require X% of edge apply latencies < 2s before marking promote 'committed' for dedicated pools.
resolution: In progress: patch PR merged to main and rolled to canary (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/2142). Early canary telemetry looks good. Plan: complete staged rollout to NovaRetail's dedicated pool by 2026-03-14, require at least 95% apply success under 2s, and recommend customer set session-token TTL >= 20s until rollout is complete. Post-rollout actions: add runbook steps to detect edge apply tail latencies and an automated guard that delays commit acknowledgement until sufficient edge nodes have applied the snapshot.
